    The four principles

    WCAG is organised as POUR. Pick a guideline to open its criteria with pass/fail examples and what to test.

    1. 1 Perceivable

      Information and UI must be presentable in ways users can perceive.

      4 guidelines · 29 criteria

      • 1.1 Text Alternatives 1
      • 1.2 Time-Based Media 9
      • 1.3 Adaptable 6
      • 1.4 Distinguishable 13

    2. 2 Operable

      UI components and navigation must be operable by everyone.

      5 guidelines · 34 criteria

      • 2.1 Keyboard Accessible 4
      • 2.2 Enough Time 6
      • 2.3 Seizures & Physical Reactions 3
      • 2.4 Navigable 13
      • 2.5 Input Modalities 8

    3. 3 Understandable

      Information and the operation of the UI must be understandable.

      3 guidelines · 21 criteria

      • 3.1 Readable 6
      • 3.2 Predictable 6
      • 3.3 Input Assistance 9

    4. 4 Robust

      Content must work reliably with a wide variety of user agents and assistive tech.

      1 guideline · 2 criteria

      • 4.1 Compatible 2

    Issue template

    The six columns I use when drafting audit findings. Copy the header row straight into a sheet.

    Issue format with a worked example
    Issue title Issue description Expected result Success criteria Conformance level Recommendation
    Product images have no text alternative The product images in the listing grid have no alt attribute, so screen readers announce the file name (e.g. "IMG_2231.jpg") or nothing at all. Each informative image has a text alternative that conveys the same information as the image. 1.1.1 Non-text Content A Add a meaningful alt describing the product (e.g. alt="Blue linen shirt, front view"). Use alt="" for purely decorative images.
